source_solutions.derivation: The largest face must be strictly less than the other two combined and the total strictly below360. First:120>100+10=110. Second:80=50+30, a degenerate equality. Third:125+120+115=360, forbidden even though each triangle inequality holds.
source_solutions.grading: Three separate yes/no parts can be reliably exact-graded after input-chain evidence, not supplied by this offline review.

source_solutions.derivation: Combine |p-q|<x<p+q, x<360-p-q, and 0<x<180. For70,80 the active upper bound150; for100,120 the active upper bound140, not180 or220. Strict endpoints exclude coplanarity. The source explicitly gives sufficiency, so every interior value exists.
source_solutions.grading: Two open intervals; must preserve degree units and both excluded endpoints. Ungraded is acceptable for unrestricted equivalent interval notation.

source_solutions.derivation: Choose three mutually perpendicular edge unit vectors e1,e2,e3. A section perpendicular to any edge has adjacent face directions equal to the remaining two perpendicular vectors. Its linear dihedral angle is90 degrees.
source_solutions.grading: One common scalar with explicit all-three qualification can be auto-graded.

source_solutions.derivation: For each angle alpha the strict face inequality gives alpha<beta+gamma=180-alpha. Thus2alpha<180 and0<alpha<90. Repeat for beta and gamma. A total180 alone for an arbitrary triangle would not imply this; the strict trihedral condition is essential.
source_solutions.grading: Proof ungraded; display must show strict inequality for every angle.

source_solutions.derivation: Noncoplanarity makes the trihedral angles at B and A nondegenerate. At B, CBD<CBA+ABD; at A, DAC<DAB+BAC. Add ACB and BDA. The bound is (ACB+CBA+BAC)+(BDA+ABD+DAB)=180+180=360, strictly.
source_solutions.grading: Proof ungraded; display must identify both local inequalities and the two triangle sums.

source_solutions.derivation: Take the common edge as z and unit vectors in the other two perpendicular face planes as u=(1/sqrt2,0,1/sqrt2),v=(0,1/sqrt2,1/sqrt2). Then u dot v=1/2. Equivalently cos(theta)=cos45 cos45+sin45 sin45 cos90=1/2, so theta60.

Take unit vectors u,v,w with pairwise dot1/2; point P=a u. Its projection onto span(v,w) is H=a(v+w)/3 because the two dot equations both equal a/2. NormH squared=a squared/3; P-H perpendicular to that plane; distance squared=2a squared/3. Equivalently the equal-radius section yields a regular tetrahedron of sidea and that tetrahedron's altitude.
source_solutions.grading: Symbolic distance cannot be marked auto without a reliable equivalence contract; ungraded display is acceptable.

source_solutions.derivation: Let the right face have orthonormal edge directions v=e1,w=e2. Opposite unit edge u has u dot v=u dot w=cos60=1/2. Its plane projection squared norm=1/4+1/4=1/2; normal component squared=1/2. The acute line-plane inclination satisfies sin(theta)=1/sqrt2, hence45, not60.

source_solutions.result: The negative polar cone {x:x dot u<=0,x dot v<=0,x dot w<=0} together with the positive equal-projection ray {t k:t>=0}, where u dot k=v dot k=w dot k=1.
source_solutions.derivation: Set S=0 and use the independent unit edge ray vectors u,v,w. Minimize ||x-t u|| squared over t>=0: t=max(0,x dot u), so ray distance squared=||x|| squared-max(0,x dot u) squared. Equal distances require all three nonnegative maxima equal. If the common maximum0, all three dot products<=0, giving the entire negative polar cone (nearest pointS for every ray). If the common maximumh>0, all three dot products=h; the invertible three-row system yields x=h k, giving exactly one positive ray. Converse follows by substituting. Origin is included. For supporting lines instead, equal absolute projections give four full lines throughS; that is a different problem and loses the polar cone.
source_solutions.grading: Open locus/proof ungraded. Source-defined ray convention resolves the issue; no arbitrary supporting-line substitution.

source_solutions.derivation: For independent unit edge vectors u,v,w the squared norm of u+v+w is3+2(cos alpha+cos beta+cos gamma). It is positive: u+v+w=0 would be a nontrivial dependence and would put the edges in one plane, not a genuine trihedral angle. Rearrangement gives the strict bound. Equality120,120,120 is coplanar and already violates total<360.
source_solutions.grading: Proof ungraded; strictness must be justified rather than replacing > by >=.

source_solutions.result: The two internal bisectors and the remaining supplementary bisector are coplanar.
source_solutions.derivation: For unit edge directions u,v,w, the bisectors of faces (u,v),(v,w) have directions u+v,v+w. A bisector of an adjacent supplement of face(u,w) has direction u-w (or its negative for the other supplement). Since u-w=(u+v)-(v+w), all three lie in the same two-dimensional span throughS. Unit normalization is necessary for unequal edge sample lengths. The internal third direction u+w generally does not lie in that span.
source_solutions.grading: Proof ungraded; display must construct the supplementary, not the third internal, bisector.

source_solutions.result: Dihedrals atSB andSD are arccos(1/3); atSA andSC are2 arccos(1/3)=arccos(-7/9).
source_solutions.derivation: Take independent unit edges a,b,c with pairwise dot1/2; d has d dot a=d dot c=1/2 and lies on the opposite side of plane(a,c) from b, because the four-faced angle is convex and B,D are distinct extreme rays. Projection of either b,d onto span(a,c) is(a+c)/3, squared norm1/3, while perpendicular components are opposite with squared length2/3. Thus b dot d=-1/3. AtB, normal-section adjacent directions a-(a dot b)b and c-(c dot b)b have cosine(1/2-1/4)/(3/4)=1/3; same atD. AtA the corresponding b,d directions give(-1/3-1/4)/(3/4)=-7/9; same atC. This is cos(2 arccos1/3), with2 arccos1/3<180. Therefore there are two values, not four equal values. Approx70.53 and141.06 degrees.
source_solutions.grading: Two pairs and exact inverse-cosine values require clear labels; ungraded is acceptable.

source_solutions.result: A cutting plane with parallelogram section always exists.
source_solutions.derivation: Take any initial bounded convex quadrilateral section A0B0C0D0 not throughS. Its diagonals intersect at interiorO. With S as origin, O=t A0+(1-t)C0=s B0+(1-s)D0,0<t,s<1. Set A'=2t A0,C'=2(1-t)C0,B'=2s B0,D'=2(1-s)D0, all on their respective positive edge rays. Then A'+C'=B'+D'=2O, so the two diagonals have common midpointO. The affine relation makes the four points coplanar; A',B',C' are noncollinear and their plane cannot containS since their edge directions are independent. The plane intersects precisely the four ordered extreme rays and bounds the convex section; the diagonals bisect each other, hence the section is a parallelogram. One cannot merely choose arbitrary equal-radius points.
source_solutions.grading: Construction/proof ungraded. Display must establish the shared positive diagonal direction, positive ray points, coplanarity and midpoint equality.
